items.title: No step-by-step timing of the local pathway
items.whyItMatters: The timing sheet records door and needle but not the steps between, so the team cannot see where to act.
items.opportunity: Add arrival-to-CT and CT-to-decision times to the timing sheet and map ten recent cases with the staff involved.

items.title: Monthly medians are too unstable at seven or eight cases a month
items.whyItMatters: Monthly summaries take five to six months to show a real change (claim c5).
items.opportunity: Plot every case on a run chart with the baseline median.

items.title: Out-of-hours patients may not benefit
items.whyItMatters: Night and weekend cases are slower and improved less elsewhere (claims c1, c3).
items.opportunity: Mark out-of-hours cases on the chart and give them their own PDSA cycle.

items.title: Faster pathways can treat more mimics
items.whyItMatters: Treated mimics rose in several reports (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Review every treated mimic and haemorrhage at the monthly meeting.

items.title: Trauma imaging could be delayed
items.whyItMatters: The CT scanner is shared with trauma.
items.opportunity: Log any trauma CT started late because of a stroke case.

reevaluation: The gaps confirm a mapping-first QI project with case-level measurement, out-of-hours attention and explicit balancing measures.
summary: Five gaps; the missing step timings are the main one.
